info.bio: Operation Ivy, nace en EEUU, para ser más específico en Oakland (Norte de California) una ciudad conflictiva situada cerca de San Francisco a finales de los 80. Sin duda alguna son parte de la familia de los padres del SKA dentro de este planeta Tierra, al igual que otras bandas como Skatalites, Rude Boys y otros. Estos chicos californianos tocaron un Ska/Punk muy bueno, siendo además pioneros en este estilo que resurgiría a mediados de los 90 con bandas como Less than Jake, Mad Caddies, Five Iron Frenzy, Goldfinger o Link 80.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Operation Ivy (1987–1989) – Skacore Pioneers; Dissolved into Rancid
podcast.body: Operation Ivy formed in 1987 and, like the Bosstones, embraced the blend of ska and hardcore known as skacore. They held it together for a couple of years and a couple of releases before dissolving and coalescing into a new band — Rancid, which became the first of the new wave of skacore bands to break out big. "Operation Ivy, they were formed in 1987 and like the muddy, muddy Boston's they were into that blend of Skah and Hardcore known as Skahcore."

podcast.title: Influence on Green Day
podcast.body: Operation Ivy was a band highly revered by a young Billy Joe Armstrong, who would later go on to form Green Day, highlighting a significant lineage within the Bay Area punk scene. "they devolved out of a band called Operation Ivy, a group that was revered by a young Billy Joe Armstrong, who of course was in Green Day"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Predecessor to Rancid
podcast.body: Operation Ivy was a hardcore punk band that began incorporating Ska into their sound as early as 1987. This group served as the direct predecessor to Rancid, playing a crucial role in the development of third-wave Ska. "That group was called Operation Ivy."

xref.title: Admiration for Rancid and Operation Ivy
xref.body: Green Day members were significant fans of both Rancid and Operation Ivy, the latter being Rancid's predecessor. Billy Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt frequently attended Operation Ivy shows at the renowned 924 Gilman Street punk club during their youth. "This pleased Green Day to no end because everyone in the band had been big fans of Ranset as well as Operation Ivy, Ranset's immediate ancestor. As kids, Billy Joe Armstrong and Mike Durant used to go see Op Ivy all the time at the infamous 924 Gilman Street punk club."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Origins and Label Strategy
xref.body: Rancid evolved from the revered band Operation Ivy and were label-mates with Bad Religion on Epitaph. Their songs were known for being short, tight, and melodic, perfectly complementing the sound kids sought after Green Day's success. They balanced punk ethics with commercial reach by remaining on Epitaph while securing distribution and quiet promotion from Warner Brothers. "Not only was Ransett label-mates with bad religion, but they devolved out of a band called Operation Ivy, a group that was revered by a young Billy Joe Armstrong, who of course was in Green Day"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dual Revival Role
xref.body: Rancid descended from the hardcore punk band Operation Ivy, which had started incorporating Ska as early as 1987. Rancid figured prominently in both the punk revival and the third wave of Ska, benefiting from the growing popularity of punk revivalists like Green Day and The Offspring. "Then came Ranset, who figured in both the punk revival and third wave SCAT. And as punk revivalists like Green Day and the offspring got bigger and bigger, Ranset was basically sucked up in their wake."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolution from Operation Ivy
xref.body: Rancid formed and evolved from Operation Ivy, a Bay Area band that preceded them in the punk scene. "They evolved out of a Bay Area band called Operation Ivy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origins and Green Day's Support
xref.body: Rancid, a Bay Area band, formed in 1991 following the disbandment of Operation Ivy, which Green Day members Billy Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt had been big fans of. As Green Day gained prominence, they actively promoted Rancid, drawing them into the mainstream spotlight. "Ranset came together in 1991 once Op Ivy disbanded after a couple of years, and as Green Day was blowing up, they chatted up Ranset whenever they could."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
